channel.title: Saleem Yousaf
channel.description: Cloud and cyber security architecture, threat analysis and governance by Saleem Yousaf.

item.title: A Curtain, Not a Cloak: What a VPN Actually Hides, and What It Leaves Wide Open
item.description: A VPN covers the network layer and nothing else. Using the Scattered Spider GDID case and the GTA 6 leaker subpoenas, a practitioner's breakdown of the three layers of identity, why Tor has the same blind spot, and what real separation would take.

item.title: Open the Door, Not the Floodgates: Running a Bug Bounty as a Defender
item.description: A bug bounty is an intake pipe you have to staff, not a control you buy. Safe harbour, scope, triage capacity, reward rubrics, and when a bounty is the right tool versus a pentest, from the programme owner's seat.

item.title: Free Streaming, Rented Address: What the Cheap TV Box Teaches Enterprise Security
item.description: Preinfected Android TV boxes run as residential proxies while you stream and as ad-fraud bots while you don't. The consumer story is only half of it. What it means for network trust, fraud controls, IoT procurement and home-office risk.

item.title: CISO 3.0: From Defender to Accountable Executive, and Where the Shift Came From
item.description: CISO 3.0 explained without the hype: the real lineage from 1.0 to 3.0, where the term is derived from, and the two forces behind it, board-level accountability and autonomous AI. What the mandate now owns, and the responsibility-versus-authority gap nobody has solved.

item.title: The Badge Still Works: Flipper Zero, RF Cloning, and the Law That Actually Applies
item.description: What handheld RF tools genuinely do, why legacy access credentials keep failing, the UK legal position on possession versus conduct, and how to run physical testing under proper authorisation.

item.title: You Shipped It. Can You Prove It? SBOM, Signing and Provenance That Actually Verify
item.description: An SBOM nobody queries is a receipt. Inventory, signing, provenance and the enforcing admission policy that turns all of it into a control, plus the delivery sequence that gets you there.

item.title: Licensed, Not Configured: Hardening Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace
item.description: The tenant is the perimeter, and both platforms ship configured for adoption rather than defence. Identity, application consent, mail forwarding, sharing defaults, and the delivery plan that closes the gaps.

item.title: Securing the CI/CD Pipeline: The Highest-Privilege System Nobody Threat Models
item.description: The pipeline deploys to production, holds every cloud credential, and executes code from anyone who can open a pull request. Trust boundaries, OIDC federation, runner isolation, SHA pinning, artefact provenance, and the delivery plan that closes the gaps.

item.title: The identifier you never chose: Windows CDP, the GDID, and how Scattered Spider got named
item.description: The Connected Devices Platform and the Global Device Identifier are convenience features that double as durable forensic evidence. How the GDID works, and how it helped name a Scattered Spider suspect.

item.title: The Global Edge: Azure Front Door, AWS CloudFront, and GCP Cloud Armor Compared
item.description: The global edge is your real internet-facing perimeter, and it is underrated. Azure Front Door, the AWS equivalent, and the GCP equivalent compared: security features, cloud and hybrid models, and setup via Terraform and the portal.

item.title: Azure Databricks and Data Factory: Use Cases and the Security Controls That Matter
item.description: A practitioner's guide to securing Azure Data Factory and Azure Databricks. Real use cases, why the data platform is a top-tier security boundary, and the identity, secrets, network, data, compute, and monitoring controls required in production.

item.title: AI Security Field Guide: Securing the LLM Stack with Open Source
item.description: A practitioner's map of the OWASP LLM Top 10 and the open source tools to test, guard, and govern the LLM stack. Prompt injection, red-teaming with garak and PyRIT, runtime guardrails, and continuous evaluation.

item.title: Post-Quantum Migration: Inventory First, Agility Second, Algorithms Last
item.description: What a post-quantum cryptography migration actually is, why harvest-now-decrypt-later makes it urgent, and the order that works: inventory first, crypto-agility second, algorithms last.

item.title: Cloud IAM and Blast Radius: Over-Privileged Roles, Least Privilege, and What Holds Up in Production
item.description: Most cloud breaches are not clever. They are an over-privileged identity doing exactly what it was allowed to do. A practitioner's take on cloud IAM, blast radius, least privilege and the guardrails that hold up in production.

item.title: Cryptographic Keys and PKI: Key Material, Rotation, and What Holds Up in Production
item.description: A practitioner's take on cryptographic keys, key material, key rotation and PKI. Why key management, not the algorithm, decides whether encryption protects anything, and the best practices that hold up in production.

item.title: FinOps: The Accountability Problem Nobody Wants to Name
item.description: FinOps programmes stall because the engineer who deploys the infrastructure never sees the bill. The tooling is fine. The accountability structure is broken. A cloud security architect's view on fixing it.

item.title: Cloud HSM: What the Vendor Documentation Skips Over
item.description: Cloud HSM gets specified for the wrong reasons. Saleem Yousaf breaks down AWS KMS, custom key store and CloudHSM direct: the real costs, and when each is right.

item.title: The Cyber Essentials Plus Pathway: What Danzell Changed, and How Remediation Programmes Actually Fail
item.description: A practitioner's guide to Cyber Essentials Plus under the Danzell question set and Requirements v3.3. The certification pathway, the five test cases, sampling mechanics, the new auto-fail rules, and the gotchas that sink remediation programmes.
